name: Wire Strippers
tagline: Remove exactly the right length of insulation without nicking the copper underneath.
parts: Adjustable length stop — repeatable strip length
Colour-coded sizing die — matches cable gauges
Hinged blades — cut insulation only, not the core
Comb/cutting jaws — trim multiple cores in one go
safety: Match the strip length to the terminal depth. Too short and the terminal eats bare copper; too long leaves exposed core beyond the screw — the classic cause of a flash between conductors.

points.label: Adjustable length stop
points.detail: A sliding gauge sets how much insulation the blade removes every time. Dial it to the terminal's stripping depth (typically 8–12 mm) and every strip comes out identical.

points.label: Colour-coded sizing die
points.detail: Each notch is a bending size, colour-marked to cable gauge (often matching the UK harmonised core colours). Squeeze to bite the insulation and rotate gently to cut it all the way around without touching the copper.

points.label: Hinged blades
points.detail: Unlike a knife, the blade depth is pre-set near the conductor diameter. The tool cuts the jacket and stops — that is what protects the strands underneath.

points.label: Comb / multi-core jaws
points.detail: The rear set of jaws nips multiple cores (or a flex) at once, so stripping a 3-core cable becomes one squeeze instead of three.
